test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-idn-003/Biolog.Features.InstitutionalIdentifiers.Tests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/quality.sh
summary: Implements BIO-IDN-003 (institutional identifiers), including both BIO-IDN-003-QA-01 closure items. AC01: InstitutionalIdentifier is typed (MATRICULATION_NUMBER/STAFF_NUMBER/TENANT_DEFINED) and every read/write resolves the tenant via ICurrentTenantProvider, never a caller-supplied id. AC02: a separate IdentifierUniquenessRule aggregate, keyed (TenantId, Type, CustomLabel), configurable via /api/v1/identifier-types/{type}/uniqueness-rule, consulted before every assignment and defaulting fail-closed to Enforced=true when unset. AC03: IdentifierStatus is a one-way ACTIVE->RETIRED transition; Value is immutable once created - a correction/reissue is a NEW record at the next SequenceNumber for the same (PersonId, Type, CustomLabel), never an in-place edit. AC04: this feature has no field, method or endpoint naming/minting/verifying a credential of any kind, proven structurally and by reflection; the identifier Value is classified 'personal' (contracts/schemas/data-classification.json) and withheld from every audit event. Applies BIO-IDN-001-QA-01 and BIO-IDN-002-QA-01 from the very first commit, not after a review round. Closes BIO-IDN-003-QA-01 (Seyi round 1, High) in full, both required-closure items from evidence/BIO-IDN-003/codex/REVIEW.md: (1) AssignAsync's per-person lock only ever serialized two callers targeting the SAME person, but AC02's enforced-uniqueness invariant spans every person in the tenant for a given (Type, CustomLabel) - fixed by acquiring IdentifierUniquenessRuleLockRegistry's (TenantId, Type, CustomLabel) lock first (the same lock and key SetRuleAsync already used, so a rule change is now also serialized against an in-flight assignment) and the narrower per-person lock second, the same two-lock-scope shape BIO-TEN-002's TenantDomainService already established. (2) enabling enforcement could silently record a rule that existing data already violated (the only way a duplicate could exist was while enforcement was off) - fixed with IInstitutionalIdentifierRepository.HasDuplicateValuesAsync, consulted by SetRuleAsync under the same lock, rejecting as uniqueness_already_violated (409) rather than persisting a broken rule.
notes: Verified end-to-end across two fix rounds: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api clean (0 warnings/errors). 55/55 feature-local unit/audit/governance tests (3 new: the cross-person race proof, the already-duplicated-scope rejection, and the clean-scope non-regression). Break-it-on-purpose verified for the concurrency fix: temporarily removed the new outer lock, confirmed the new test failed with the predicted symptom (both callers succeeded, two records stored), restored and re-confirmed green. 64/64 dotnet integration tests (unaffected). 154/154 dotnet unit tests (unaffected). BIO-IDN-001 (70/70) and BIO-IDN-002 (47/47) feature-local regressions unaffected. 63/63 offline structural checks (7 new QA-01 checks across both closure items). dotnet vulnerability audit clean. contract-freeze PASS. traceability PASS. module-reference-direction PASS.
